Hi Elaine — thanks for the sample, this is helpful. Below is a concise sizing recommendation with the assumptions called out. We can refine during a quick call — proposing Thurs 09/19 11:00 PT if that works.

Quick summary (ballpark):
- Peak token demand (observed spike): 120 QPS * 400 tokens = 48,000 tokens/sec
- Candidate model variants we recommend testing in pilot: rw-13B (int8 quantized) and rw-13B (fp16) — int8 gives ~35–50% better throughput at minimal quality loss for most instruction-following tasks.

Estimated sustained tokens/sec per GPU (observed on Redwood Dedicated configs):
- rw-13B fp16: ~2,800 tok/s per A100-equivalent GPU
- rw-13B int8: ~4,200 tok/s per A100-equivalent GPU
- rw-70B int8: ~950 tok/s per GPU (included for capacity comparison only)

Sizing math (peak):
- If we run rw-13B int8: required GPUs = ceil(48,000 / 4,200) = 12 GPUs
- If we run rw-13B fp16: required GPUs = ceil(48,000 / 2,800) = 18 GPUs

Headroom and operational guidance:
- Add nominal 25–33% headroom to cover short spikes, background maintenance, and KV-cache warmup. That pushes the int8 recommendation to ~15–16 GPUs (we typically recommend reserving the next slab size).
- We recommend an autoscale buffer (burst) to cover rare >5-minute sustained overage; pilot can use burst credits or a small node pool of 4 GPUs.

Latency expectation (generation-only, ballpark):
- For rw-13B int8 at 4,200 tok/s, a 150-token generation is ~36ms generation time; add decoding, RPC and small model overhead (~60–100ms) => p95 ~120–160ms in warmed steady-state.
- With end-to-end network and client processing we expect p95 to remain under your 250ms target in the warmed path. Cold starts or heavy queueing could push this higher, so the headroom buffer is important.

Next steps:
1) Quick tech call to confirm dataset/peak windows and any long-context runs (do you have frequent requests >1k tokens?).
2) Pilot config: reserve 16 A100-equivalent GPUs running rw-13B int8, enable prefix KV caching, set autoscale burst of 4 GPUs.
3) We’ll provide a short SLA addendum for the pilot and a cost estimate tied to the reserved slab + expected burst usage.

Attaching a short proposal (redwood-sla-proposal-v1.pdf). Happy to walk through the numbers on the call.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Elaine — following our internal validation, attaching the pilot SLA and a concise sizing appendix. Summary below and next steps to get the pilot scheduled.

Final recommended pilot configuration (conservative):
- Reserved slab: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs running rw-13B int8
- Burst pool: 4 GPUs for short sustained spikes (automated scaling policy)
- Expected behavior at peak: 48,000 tok/s demand -> steady capacity coverage with 16 GPUs + burst for >2–3 minute sustained overshoots
- Latency: warmed p95 generation-only ~40–60ms for 150-token outputs; end-to-end p95 expected ~120–180ms (meets your 250ms target)
- Operational notes: enable KV/prefix caching for conversational flows; pre-warm top 50 prompts from your sample during the first 24 hours of pilot to reduce cold tails

Costs and SLA addendum are in the attached redwood-sla-proposal-v1.pdf. If the configuration looks good I’ll route the DocuSign link (we can enable a small trial credit for the first week) and book the pilot start for 2026-10-04.
